text: Repositories work with any standard Git client over HTTPS or SSH
quote: GitCafe repositories work with any Git client over HTTPS or SSH.

text: Pull requests let you browse files, compare diffs, and leave feedback next to the code
quote: Browse files, compare diffs, and leave feedback alongside the code.

text: Stack pull requests on top of an open PR, review each change separately, and merge the stack in order
quote: Build on an open pull request. Review each change separately, then merge the stack in order.

text: A CLI command pushes each commit as its own branch with one PR per commit, and works with Git, jj and Sapling
quote: `cafe stack submit` pushes each commit after the base as its own branch and opens or reuses one pull request per commit. Run it from your checkout; it works with Git, jj and Sapling.

text: Landing merges a stack from the bottom up through a chosen pull request
quote: Landing merges the stack from the bottom up through the pull request you choose.

text: Stack actions include Land, Restack, Unstack and Close stack, with live progress of landing and restacking
quote: offers **Land**, **Restack**, **Unstack** and **Close stack** with the live progress of the latest landing and restack.

text: Import GitHub repositories along with their issues, pull requests, reviews and comments
quote: Bring repositories from GitHub into GitCafe with their issues, pull requests, reviews and comments, and optionally keep both sides in sync.

text: Keep code, issues and pull requests in sync with GitHub, either one way or both ways
quote: Import from GitHub and keep code, issues, and pull requests in sync, one way or both.

text: Mirror a branch with another Git server
quote: Mirror a branch with another Git server

text: Sign up by choosing Sync with GitHub and approving GitCafe on GitHub
quote: On the sign-up page, choose **Sync with GitHub** and approve GitCafe on GitHub.

text: Repositories created in GitCafe do not need a GitHub account
quote: GitHub is optional: repositories created in GitCafe need no GitHub account.

text: New accounts created from GitHub get the SSH and GPG keys from the GitHub profile, with default SSH access
quote: Your new account also gets the SSH and GPG keys on your GitHub profile, with the default SSH access; keys GitCafe cannot use are skipped.

text: The Cafe CLI handles sign-in and Git credential setup, and manages repositories, PRs, stacks and issues from the terminal
quote: It signs you in, sets up Git credentials, and manages repositories, pull requests, stacks, issues and more from the terminal.

text: Agent skills give coding assistants the same GitCafe workflow
quote: Add agent skills to give your coding assistant the same workflow.

text: The CLI supports JSON output, non-interactive mode and auto-confirmation for scripted or headless use
quote: `--json` prints structured output; progress and errors go to stderr. `--no-input` fails instead of prompting; `--yes` confirms destructive actions.

text: The CLI can send authenticated requests to any REST API endpoint
quote: `cafe api <path>` sends an authenticated request to any REST API endpoint.

text: The API description is available as OpenAPI 3.1 JSON for code generators
quote: The same description is available as OpenAPI 3.1 JSON for code generators

text: Resending an API request with the same requestId returns the original result instead of repeating the operation
quote: If the response is lost, send the same request with the same `requestId` again: you get the original result instead of a second operation.

text: Webhooks send signed HTTPS requests on repository or organization events such as pushes, new issues and merged PRs
quote: A webhook sends a signed HTTPS request to your server when something happens in a repository or organization, such as a push, a new issue or a merged pull request.

text: Buildkite builds appear on a repository CI tab and as checks on pull requests
quote: GitCafe shows Buildkite builds on a repository's **CI** tab and as checks on pull requests.

text: GitHub Actions results arrive as checks
quote: GitHub Actions results arrive as checks.

text: For GitHub-synced repositories, pipeline results can be published to GitHub as checks
quote: For a repository synchronized with GitHub, you can publish each pipeline's results to GitHub as checks.

text: Rulesets protect branches or tags by requiring PRs, reviews and passing checks, or by blocking deletion and force pushes
quote: A ruleset protects matching branches or tags: it can require pull requests, reviews and passing checks, or block deletion and force pushes.

text: Rulesets have an evaluate mode that only produces warnings, so rules can be tried before enforcement
quote: **Evaluate**: the rules only produce warnings, so you can try them first.

text: Changed paths can require approval from their owners listed in CODEOWNERS
quote: **Code owners**: each changed path needs approval from one of its owners in `CODEOWNERS`

text: Personal access tokens with granted permissions only, for the REST API or Git over HTTPS, and they always expire
quote: A personal access token lets scripts, CI jobs and tools use the REST API or Git over HTTPS as you, with only the permissions you grant. Tokens start with `gct_` and always expire.

text: Access can be limited to selected repositories instead of all accessible ones
quote: Choose the repository access: **All repositories you can access** (the default...) or **Only select repositories…**

text: A hosted MCP server lets AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT read repositories and, with approval, work on issues and PRs
quote: GitCafe runs an MCP server at `https://git.cafe/mcp`, so AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT can read repositories and, with your approval, work on issues and pull requests.

text: MCP read tools work on public repositories without connecting an account
quote: Without connecting an account, its read tools work on public repositories: code, branches and tags, issues, pull requests, reviews and CI results.

text: In browsers that support WebMCP, GitCafe pages expose the MCP server's tools to the browser's agent
quote: In a browser that supports WebMCP, GitCafe pages offer the MCP server's tools to the browser's agent.

text: Guides and most repository pages can be read as Markdown for scripts and coding agents
quote: Every guide, and most repository pages, can be read as Markdown. This is handy for scripts, coding agents and anything that prefers text to HTML.

text: Each repository provides an llms.txt overview
quote: A repository's `/<owner>/<repo>/llms.txt` gives an overview of that repository.

text: Track work with issues that support pinning, locking, labels and milestones
quote: Track work with issues, pin and lock, labels and milestones.

text: View commit history, inspect individual commits, and see line-by-line blame
quote: Read a repository's commit history, inspect a single commit, and see who last changed each line of a file.

text: Hand an issue or PR to an external coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Amp from a button
quote: The button next to an issue or pull request number hands it to a coding agent. Its menu lists Amp, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and T3 Code

text: Private repositories are free during the public beta, and paid plans raise limits
quote: Private repositories are free during the public beta; paid plans add higher limits.
